title: Business Travelers Just Want Some Time Alone
paragraphs: Business trips can sound exciting: a new city, a few days away from the office and meals paid for by the company.
But after a long day of meetings, many travelers seem to want just one thing: to close the hotel room door and be left alone.
A new US survey has found that nine in 10 business travelers said their hotel room was the only place where they really felt "off the clock" during a work trip.

The survey, done by Talker Research for Hyatt, included 2,000 Americans who travel regularly for work. It asked people about their experiences on business trips and what they do to get a little time to themselves.

Nearly half said they had gone back to their hotel room instead of networking. More than a third had pretended they had meetings to get some quiet time, while a similar number had pretended to have another commitment so they could avoid a dinner.

But the time they spend in their room is not completely work-free, either. More than half said they worked on most nights after the official workday had ended, and another 22% said they worked every night while traveling.

Still, relaxing in their hotel room was what travelers looked forward to the most on a business trip, so it's no surprise they care about hotel quality. Nine in 10 said their hotel could "make or break" a trip, while eight in 10 said a high-quality hotel helped them work better.
But travelers weren't asking for anything too fancy. Their top hotel must-haves were a comfortable bed, good Wi-Fi, 24-hour food service, free breakfast and early check-in.
So while many travelers see a hotel room as just a place to sleep, for business travelers it may be the most exciting part of the trip!
